# Deprecations

> For the complete documentation index, see llms.txt. Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to the page URL.

## Overview

As we launch safer and more capable models, we regularly retire older models. Software relying on OpenAI models may need occasional updates to keep working. Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in our documentation along with blog posts for larger changes.

This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements.

To monitor model shutdowns programmatically, call the List models endpoint (`GET /v1/models`) and check each model's optional `shutdown_date` field. When present, this field contains the shutdown date as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, or `null` if no shutdown date has been announced; the field is also available from the Retrieve a model endpoint.

## Model deprecation notice periods

We provide advance notice before retiring models so customers have time to plan and migrate. When we announce a model deprecation, we notify customers who are actively using the model by email and document the deprecation on this page.

Unless safety or compliance concerns require a faster timeline, we provide the following minimum notice periods before model retirement:

- Generally available models: At least 6 months.
- Specialized variants of generally available models: At least 3 months. Examples include chat variants such as `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, Codex variants such as `gpt-5.3-codex`, and deep research variants such as `o3-deep-research`.
- Preview models: Preview models, identified by `preview` in the model name, may be retired with much shorter notice, such as 2 weeks. Examples include `computer-use-preview` and `gpt-4o-audio-preview`. We don't recommend using preview models for business-critical production workloads unless you can migrate on short notice.

If safety or compliance concerns require us to retire a model sooner, we will provide as much notice as reasonably possible.

These notice periods give customers time to evaluate recommended replacement models, test application behavior, and complete migrations before a model is no longer available. In some cases, developers may be able to provision dedicated capacity for continued access after a model's shutdown date. To explore this option, contact our sales team.

## Deprecation vs. legacy

We use the term "deprecation" to refer to the process of retiring a model or endpoint. When we announce that a model or endpoint is being deprecated, it immediately becomes deprecated. All deprecated models and endpoints will also have a shut down date. At the time of the shut down, the model or endpoint will no longer be accessible.

We use the terms "sunset" and "shut down" interchangeably to mean a model or endpoint is no longer accessible.

We use the term "legacy" to refer to models and endpoints that no longer receive updates. We tag endpoints and models as legacy to signal to developers where we're moving as a platform and that they should likely migrate to newer models or endpoints. You can expect that a legacy model or endpoint will be deprecated at some point in the future.

## Upcoming deprecations

Upcoming deprecations are listed below, with the most recent announcements at the top.

### 2026-10-14: GPT-4 series model deprecations

On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

| Shutdown date | Model / system | Recommended replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| January 14, 2027 | GPT-4o (`gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`) | `gpt-6-luna` |
| January 14, 2027 | GPT-4o mini (`gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`) | `gpt-6-luna` |
| January 14, 2027 | GPT-4.1 (`gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`) | `gpt-6-luna` |
| January 14, 2027 | GPT-4.1 mini (`gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`) | `gpt-6-luna` |

Retiring GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT | OpenAI

January 29, 2026

# Retiring GPT‑4o, GPT‑4.1, GPT‑4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT

On February 13, 2026, alongside the previously announced retirement⁠ of GPT‑5 (Instant and Thinking), we will retire GPT‑4o, GPT‑4.1, GPT‑4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini from ChatGPT. In the API, there are no changes at this time.

While this announcement applies to several older models, GPT‑4o deserves special context.

After we first deprecated it and later restored access during the GPT‑5 release, we learned more about how people actually use it day to day. We brought GPT‑4o back after hearing clear feedback from a subset of Plus and Pro users, who told us they needed more time to transition key use cases, like creative ideation, and that they preferred GPT‑4o’s conversational style and warmth.

That feedback directly shaped GPT‑5.1 and GPT‑5.2, with improvements to personality, stronger support for creative ideation, and more ways to customize how ChatGPT responds⁠(opens in a new window). You can choose from base styles and tones like Friendly, and controls for things like warmth and enthusiasm. Our goal is to give people more control and customization over how ChatGPT feels to use—not just what it can do.

We’re announcing the upcoming retirement of GPT‑4o today because these improvements are now in place, and because the vast majority of usage has shifted to GPT‑5.2, with only 0.1% of users still choosing GPT‑4o each day.

More broadly, we’re continuing to improve ChatGPT across areas users have told us need work. This includes further improvements to personality and creativity, as well as addressing unnecessary refusals and overly cautious or preachy responses, with updates coming soon. We’re continuing to make progress toward a version of ChatGPT designed for adults over 18, grounded in the principle of treating adults like adults, and expanding user choice and freedom within appropriate safeguards. To support this, we’ve rolled out age prediction⁠(opens in a new window) for users under 18 in most markets.

Changes like this take time to adjust to, and we’ll always be clear about what’s changing and when. We know that losing access to GPT‑4o will feel frustrating for some users, and we didn’t make this decision lightly. Retiring models is never easy, but it allows us to focus on improving the models most people use today.

GPT-4o deprecated? — shutdown date & replacement

# GPT-4o (OpenAI) 

 No — GPT-4o is not deprecated as of July 30, 2026. OpenAI has announced neither a deprecation nor a shutdown date for it. 

 The omni model that made multimodal input routine and halved the price of GPT-4 Turbo at the same time. It is still the default many production stacks reach for, and OpenAI has kept the floating gpt-4o pointer alive even as the dated snapshot behind it changed. The May 2024 snapshot is deprecated; the pointer itself is not. 

## The facts

| Provider | OpenAI |
| --- | --- |
| Model id | gpt-4o |
| Released | May 13, 2024 |
| Deprecated | not deprecated |
| Shutdown | not published |
| Status | Active |
| Last verified | July 30, 2026 |

Is OpenAI GPT-4o still available?

Yes. OpenAI GPT-4o is active and fully supported as of July 30, 2026.

## Models that migrate here

 OpenAI names GPT-4o as the replacement for 3 models. 

- code-davinci-002
- gpt-4-32k
- gpt-4-vision-preview

## This page, for machines

Drop the badge in a README so it turns red the day this model is retired:

```
[![gpt-4o](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://modeldeprecations.dev/badge/openai/gpt-4o.json)](https://modeldeprecations.dev/openai/gpt-4o)
```

```
# How to use modeldeprecations.dev

[modeldeprecations.dev](https://modeldeprecations.dev) answers one question per model: is it deprecated,
when does it shut down, and what replaces it. Every date on the site is cited to the
provider's own documentation, with the date we last checked it.

Three lifecycle states are used, matching the providers' own vocabulary:

- **active** — still supported, no deprecation announced.
- **deprecated** — the provider has announced it is going away. It still answers requests.
- **retired** — API access is gone. Requests fail.

A model can be active *and* carry a shutdown date: Anthropic publishes a
"not sooner than" date and Google publishes an earliest shutdown date for models
that are current and fully supported. Those are reported as scheduled shutdowns,
not deprecations, because that is what the provider actually committed to.

## Check one model

```bash
curl https://modeldeprecations.dev/api/v1/models/openai/gpt-4-32k.json
```

Or fetch the page as Markdown, which includes the answer, the dates and the sources:

```bash
curl https://modeldeprecations.dev/openai/gpt-4-32k.md
```

## Full catalog

```bash
curl https://modeldeprecations.dev/api/v1/models.json
```

Ids are `provider/model`. Dated snapshots (`gpt-4-32k-0613`) are listed as aliases of
their canonical entry rather than as separate records.

Each entry carries `computed_status`, the lifecycle state recomputed against the build
date — so a model whose shutdown has passed reads `retired` without anyone editing data.

## Badges

A shields.io endpoint per model, for READMEs that should go red when a model dies:

```
https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://modeldeprecations.dev/badge/openai/gpt-4-32k.json
```

## Calendar and changelog

- Subscribe to every shutdown date: https://modeldeprecations.dev/calendar.ics
- Changelog RSS: https://modeldeprecations.dev/changelog.xml

## JSON Schema

```bash
curl https://modeldeprecations.dev/api/v1/schema.json
```

## Contribute

Data lives in YAML under `models/{provider}/{model}.yaml` in the
[GitHub repo](https://github.com/mnfst/modeldeprecations.dev). Every lifecycle date needs a source URL; CI rejects a
date without one. Open a PR.

## For agents

- Machine-readable overview: https://modeldeprecations.dev/llms.txt
- This guide plus every model inline: https://modeldeprecations.dev/llms-full.txt
- Any page also exists as Markdown: append `.md` to a model URL.
- In a browser, this site registers a **WebMCP** tool on `navigator.modelContext`:
 `check_model_deprecation`, `list_shutdowns`, `find_replacement`, and `get_usage_guide`.
- Parameters each model accepts are catalogued on the sibling site, https://modelparams.dev.

# GPT-4o retirement: replacement options and migration checks

The dated GPT-4o API snapshot has an October 23, 2026 retirement date. Compare the official replacement with lower-cost options that fit the same workload.

By benchr Editorial Team · Updated September 11, 2026 · Verified against OpenAI's deprecation docs, June 12, 2026 · View changelog

Snapshot as of June 12, 2026; GPT-5.6 options added September 11, 2026. GPT-4o goes down with eight other model IDs; the full wave is on the October 2026 retirements page.

Short answer: The recorded retirement date for gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is October 23, 2026. OpenAI's recorded replacement is GPT-5.5, whose listed output price is higher. benchr's editorial cost match is GPT-5 at $1.25/$10; call the `gpt-5` alias, because the dated `gpt-5-2025-08-07` snapshot shuts down December 11, 2026. For the current generation, benchr points general work at GPT-5.6 Terra ($2/$12) and high-volume traffic at GPT-5.6 Luna ($0.20/$1.20). Compare candidates on the same prompts, modalities, endpoint requirements, and production constraints before routing traffic.

Shutdown date 2026, announced April GPT-4o input / 1M 2024-05-13 snapshot GPT-5 input / 1M benchr's value pick Production lifespan May 2024 → Oct 2026

## Who needs to migrate

GPT-4o launched May 13, 2024 with voice and vision support. OpenAI later changed its availability in ChatGPT, then partly reversed that change after user objections. That ChatGPT history is separate from the API retirement schedule below.

The API follows a separate schedule. OpenAI's current deprecation table sets the retirement date for the launch snapshot; requests to that exact ID are scheduled to fail after October 23.

## Read your model string carefully

The retirement names `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` — the original launch snapshot, which billed $5 input / $15 output per million tokens. Later snapshots billed differently, and bare aliases like `gpt-4o` resolve to whatever OpenAI currently points them at. Two practical consequences:

First, if you pinned the May 2024 snapshot for output consistency, you've been paying 2024 prices for two years. Whatever you migrate to, you'll likely spend less per token. Second, don't assume an alias saves you. Audit which snapshot your traffic resolves to in the usage dashboard, because "it still works today" tells you nothing about October 24.

## Replacement options and listed prices

GPT-4o replacement options (per 1M tokens, verified June 12, 2026; GPT-5.6 rows added September 11, 2026)

| Option | Input | Output | Pick it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-5.5 (OpenAI's official pick) | $5.00 | $30.00 | Agentic work, computer use, 1M context: the loads GPT-4o was never good at anyway |
| GPT-5 (benchr's cost pick) | $1.25 | $10.00 | Chat, drafting, summarization, everyday vision: the actual GPT-4o workload |
| GPT-5.6 Terra (benchr's current-generation pick) | $2.00 | $12.00 | You want OpenAI's current general tier and a 1.05M window; costs more than GPT-5 on both sides |
| GPT-5.6 Luna | $0.20 | $1.20 | High-volume classification, routing, extraction where 4o was overkill; cheaper than GPT-5 Mini on both sides, with a 1.05M window |
| GPT-5 Mini | $0.25 | $2.00 | You already run it and its 400K window is enough |

The official migration path points up-market, which is how provider migration paths usually point. Price the workload instead. Most GPT-4o traffic is conversational and short-form; GPT-5 handles it at a quarter of 4o's original input price and two-thirds of its output price, and the GPT-5 pricing page shows the monthly math at real volumes. results.text:
GPT-4o API Deprecation: Migration Guide

# OpenAI is retiring GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 API snapshots: migrate without regressions

A source-led production migration plan for the GPT-4-series API shutdown, covering exact model inventory, compatibility evidence, fine-tuned routes and reversible rollout.

Noor Yasser 14 October 2026 9 min read

An editorial interpretation of the topic, followed by a practical execution diagram.

ON THIS PAGE

OpenAI announced on 14 October 2026 that five dated GPT-4-series API snapshots will be removed on 14 January 2027: two GPT-4o snapshots, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini. OpenAI recommends GPT-6 Luna for all five. The practical response is not a one-line model-name replacement: inventory every production route, freeze a representative test set, version the complete request contract, compare outputs and tool behavior, then ship through shadow traffic and a reversible canary. This matters to teams running structured extraction, tool calling, customer support, content workflows or fine-tuned GPT-4 descendants—especially because fine-tuned versions inherit the same shutdown date.

The official OpenAI deprecations page is the source of record for the announcement and dates. It lists `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` and `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14` for shutdown on 14 January 2027, with `gpt-6-luna` as the recommended replacement. Those model IDs, dates and replacement are documented facts. The testing, routing and rollout plan below is engineering analysis for reducing migration risk; OpenAI has not claimed that every application will behave identically after changing the model.

## What exactly is being retired

The notice targets explicit dated snapshots, not an abstract product family. That distinction matters because production systems often hide model IDs behind aliases, environment variables, prompt-management tools, SDK defaults, batch jobs, fine-tuning job outputs or a vendor gateway. Search configuration, code, observability dimensions and deployment manifests for the exact IDs. Also inspect stored request templates and scheduled workers that may run less often than the main API path.

Build one inventory row per route: owner, endpoint, model ID, snapshot or fine-tuned model, prompt version, schema version, tools, traffic, data class, latency SLO, fallback, last successful request and removal deadline. Treat an unresolved row as operational debt. A dashboard showing only the visible model name is insufficient if the actual request is rewritten by a gateway.

Fine-tuned models need a separate branch in the plan. OpenAI states that fine-tuned versions of the listed models follow the same shutdown schedule as their base models. The GPT-6 Luna model page currently marks fine-tuning as unsupported. Therefore, do not assume that an existing fine-tuned model can be recreated directly on Luna. Recover the original training and validation data, document the behavior the fine-tune supplied, test whether prompting, retrieval or deterministic code can replace it, and choose another supported path only after verifying current official documentation.

## The migration unit is the request contract

Changing only `model` ignores the parts most likely to cause regressions. Version the model together with instructions, message roles, reasoning effort, tool definitions, JSON Schema, response parser, retry policy, timeouts, safety checks, conversation-state strategy and cost or latency budgets. A release should point to one immutable contract bundle so the old and new paths can be replayed and compared.

The GPT-6 Luna documentation describes a 1.05-million-token context window, 128,000 maximum output tokens, text and image input, Structured Outputs, function calling and reasoning-effort controls. # Retiring GPT-4o and other ChatGPT models

GPT-4o and additional models were deprecated in ChatGPT on February 13, 2026. These models will continue to be available in the API.

Updated: last month

## Overview

As of February 13, 2026, ChatGPT retired the following models:

GPT-4o

GPT-4.1

GPT-4.1 mini

OpenAI o4-mini

GPT-5 (Instant and Thinking), as previously announced

As of March 11, 2026, ChatGPT retired the following models:

GPT-5.1 Instant

GPT-5.1 Thinking

GPT-5.1 Pro

ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces will retain access to GPT-5 models through February 19, 2026. GPT-5 Pro will also remain available to all paid users through February 19.

## What’s changing

These models will no longer be available for use in ChatGPT.GPT-5.1 models were retired on March 11, 2026 across both normal chats and GPTs.They will continue to be available through the OpenAI API, and we’ll provide advance notice ahead of any future API retirements.ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers will retain access to GPT-4o within Custom GPTs until April 3, 2026. After April 3, GPT-4o will be fully retired across all plans.

## Learn more

For additional background on this decision and what’s coming next, please refer to our blog post: Retiring GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT

## FAQ

### What happens to my conversations I have with GPT-4o or other deprecated models?

Conversations and projects are defaulted to their GPT-5.3 Instant and GPT-5.4 Thinking and Pro equivalents going forward.

### What happens to my GPTs?

GPTs using retired models will automatically move to the closest GPT-5.3 Instant and GPT-5.4 Thinking and Pro equivalent.

### Will voice mode still run on GPT-4o?

ChatGPT Voice is not changing as part of this update. While voice uses a similar base model as GPT-4o, it’s ultimately a different model from the text GPT-4o model being retired.

### Will ChatGPT Images still run on GPT-4o?

ChatGPT Images is not changing as part of this update. While image generation uses a similar base model as GPT-4o, it’s ultimately a different model from the text GPT-4o model being retired.

OpenAI Model Shutdown Oct 23: Migration Guide | Zentor Blog

# OpenAI Model Shutdown Oct 23: Migration Guide 

 1 min read · October 13, 2026 · Zentor Editorial 

OpenAI model deprecation hits GPT-4, o1 and o4-mini API IDs on Oct 23, 2026. Check the affected aliases, replacement models and a practical migration plan.

Contents

OpenAI model deprecation now has a dated cutoff: its API deprecations notice schedules older GPT-4, o1, o3-mini and o4-mini identifiers for shutdown on October 23, 2026. An app that still sends one of those identifiers needs an explicit replacement and a tested rollout; changing a model name without checking its outputs, tools and access is not a migration. As of October 13, the notice lists 12 entries in its main October table and five additional fine-tuned model families in a separate table, with several bare aliases covered by those entries.

Key Takeaways:

- Search both dated snapshots and bare names such as `gpt-4` and `o4-mini`; OpenAI lists affected aliases next to the snapshots.
- Match each old identifier to the replacement on OpenAI's page. There is no one-size-fits-all GPT-5.6 target.
- Treat a missing model as a request failure, not a signal to silently pick another model.
- Fine-tuned behavior does not transfer when you replace a base model. Check training eligibility before planning another fine-tune.

## Which OpenAI models shut down on October 23?

As of October 13, 2026, the April 22 legacy-model entry schedules these API identifiers for October 23: `gpt-3.5-turbo-0125`, `gpt-4-0613`, `gpt-4-1106-preview`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `gpt-image-1`, `o1-2024-12-17`, `o1-pro-2025-03-19`, `o3-mini-2025-01-31`, `ft-o4-mini-2025-04-16` and `o4-mini-2025-04-16`. The same entry names aliases, including `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3-mini` and `o4-mini`. Read the table's alias column rather than searching only for year-stamped strings.

One wrinkle is worth flagging: the page also lists `gpt-4-1106-preview` under an earlier March 2026 shutdown. Its October appearance should not be read as evidence that a March-removed model works today. Confirm actual availability for your project instead of relying on either row to infer present access.

OpenAI's public deprecations page, showing its explanation of model retirement and notice periods

## What happens when an old model stops answering?

OpenAI defines shutdown as the point when a model or endpoint is no longer accessible. Its Agents API error guide documents HTTP 404 with `model_not_found` when a requested model is unavailable; the general error guide maps a missing resource to `NotFoundError` in the Python library. Neither guide promises a particular error message or status for every endpoint, SDK and project. Don't hard-code a quoted error string as your only alert.

Suppose an evening report calls `o4-mini` through a saved workflow while its owner changes the model in a different dashboard. That other change doesn't repair the saved workflow. Log the actual requested model and error code, route the failure to its owner, and verify that the replacement was selected deliberately. The official deprecation notice offers replacement recommendations, not a promise of automatic forwarding.

OpenAI's Agents API errors page, showing where to inspect request errors and structured error codes

## Use OpenAI's replacement mapping, not a bulk rename

The October table maps the GPT-4 family, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `o1` and `o3-mini` to `gpt-5.6-sol`. It directs `gpt-3.5-turbo` and `o4-mini` to `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-4.1-nano` to `gpt-5.6-luna`, and `gpt-image-1` to either `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. For `o1-pro`, the table specifically names `gpt-5.6-sol` with `reasoning.mode: pro`. These are recommendations as of October 13, 2026; check the live notice again when deploying.

OpenAI Model Deprecation Dates: What Shuts Down When | MadRobot

# OpenAI API shutdown dates: o4-mini, o3-mini, o1 and GPT-4 Turbo stop working on October 23

 Sanjit Patel Oct 4 2026 - 00:47 UTC Updated Oct 13 2026 - 12:42 UTC 

OpenAI’s wordmark. Image: OpenAI (wordmark, public domain via Wikimedia Commons)

OpenAI will shut down a batch of older models in its API on October 23, 2026, including o1, o1-pro, o3-mini, o4-mini, GPT-4 Turbo, the original GPT-4, gpt-4o-2024-05-13, gpt-4.1-nano and gpt-3.5-turbo-0125. After that date, apps that still call them stop working. The dates are on OpenAI’s deprecations page, and OpenAI says customers who are actively using a model are told by email.

More shutdowns follow in November and December, then into 2027, including GPT-5.1. Below is every upcoming date, the model OpenAI suggests in each case, and what to do now.

Jump to:

- OpenAI models shutting down on October 23, 2026
- Later OpenAI deprecation dates (November 2026 to April 2027)
- What does deprecated mean, and how much notice do you get?
- What to do if you got the deprecation email
- What isn’t affected: ChatGPT and Azure
- FAQ

## OpenAI models shutting down on October 23, 2026

OpenAI announced this batch on April 22, 2026, saying it wanted “to improve reliability and make it easier for developers to choose the right models”. The page lists the short names alongside the dated snapshots, so code that calls `o4-mini` rather than `o4-mini-2025-04-16` is affected too.

| Model (and names listed with it) | Shuts down | OpenAI’s substitute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `o4-mini-2025-04-16`, `o4-mini` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| `o3-mini-2025-01-31`, `o3-mini` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `o1-2024-12-17`, `o1` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `o1-pro-2025-03-19`, `o1-pro` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` (reasoning mode pro) |
| `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `gpt-4-0613`, `gpt-4` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-nano` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `gpt-3.5-turbo-0125`, `gpt-3.5-turbo` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| `gpt-image-1` | Oct 23, 2026 | `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` |

From OpenAI’s deprecations page. The page also lists the “-completions” versions of GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo.

Fine-tuned models built on these go on the same day: fine-tunes of GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, gpt-4.1-nano, o4-mini, babbage-002 and davinci-002. OpenAI says inference on fine-tuned models keeps working only until the base model is deprecated, and suggests rebuilding on gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-sol or gpt-5.6-luna.

# GPT-4o, o1, and o3-mini on OpenAI's October 23 shutdown list

> OpenAI shuts down gpt-4o-2024-05-13, o1, and o3-mini on October 23. Azure's dates are December 9 and November 19. Inventory, test, and switch with records.

- Published: 2026-10-13
- Last reviewed: 2026-10-13
- Data as of: 2026-10-13
- Article slug: openai-october-23-shutdown
- Author: Glevd
- Reading time: 8 minutes
- Topics: model-retirement, openai, gpt-4o, azure, migration, api
- Canonical URL: https://benchlm.ai/blog/posts/openai-october-23-shutdown

OpenAI's deprecations page lists October 23, 2026 as the API shutdown date for `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `o1` (including `o1-2024-12-17`), and `o3-mini` (including `o3-mini-2025-01-31`).

On Azure, Microsoft's schedule dates the same models differently: December 9 for GPT-4o version 2024-05-13, and November 19 for o1 and o3-mini.

OpenAI names `gpt-5.6-sol` as the replacement for all three. Microsoft names `gpt-5.6-sol` for GPT-4o and o1, and `gpt-5.6-terra` for o3-mini.

Your first decision is which of those dates applies to your code. We re-read both sources on October 13.

## Your deadline is set by the platform and the exact ID

Evidence: OpenAI's deprecations page, the "Legacy GPT model snapshots" section announced April 22, 2026, and Microsoft's retirement schedule, both read October 13, 2026. The rows below come from our lifecycle feed, captured 2026-10-13.

| Exact model ID | Serving route | Published date | Named replacement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-4o-2024-05-13 | OpenAI API | 2026-10-23 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| gpt-4o@2024-05-13 | Azure AI Foundry | 2026-12-09 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o1 | OpenAI API | 2026-10-23 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o1-2024-12-17 | OpenAI API | 2026-10-23 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o1@2024-12-17 | Azure AI Foundry | 2026-11-19 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o3-mini | OpenAI API | 2026-10-23 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o3-mini-2025-01-31 | OpenAI API | 2026-10-23 | gpt-5.6-sol |
| o3-mini@2025-01-31 | Azure AI Foundry | 2026-11-19 | gpt-5.6-terra |

Published dates for three model lookups, shown separately for the OpenAI API and Azure. These are provider dates, not observed outages.

Read the table by the string your code sends. `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` on the OpenAI API is October 23. Our feed labels the Azure version of the same snapshot `gpt-4o@2024-05-13`, and it runs to December 9. Each of o1 and o3-mini has an alias and a dated snapshot on OpenAI's side, all dated October 23, and one Azure version dated November 19. Our per-model pages keep the receipts: gpt-4o-2024-05-13, o1, and o3-mini.

Other GPT-4o IDs aren't on this date. OpenAI's table lists no October 23 row for `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, or `gpt-4o-mini`, and Azure lists April 14, 2027 for the two later GPT-4o versions. Audio, realtime, and transcribe IDs carry January 20 and February 26, 2027 dates. Missing dates aren't a promise to keep a model. They mean the table gives none as of October 13.

OpenAI dates more than these three on October 23. Our feed counts 29 first-party rows with that date, and 24 of them are outside this article, including `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4-0613`, `o1-pro`, `o4-mini`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-image-1`, and six fine-tuned model IDs. If any of those show up in your inventory, the OpenAI deprecation calendar lists their replacements, and Azure's own dates are on a separate page.

## Model IDs are set in more places than the chat setting

Dashboards rarely show the only model in use. Search these places: environment variables and config files, default arguments in a shared SDK wrapper, scheduled jobs and queue workers that deploy separately, gateways with fallback chains, evaluation notebooks, and vendor tools configured with your key. Saved batch input files need their own pass, because each request line names its model. Last month's file still names whatever you chose last month.

Dave Kurian
Posted on Oct 13 • Originally published at otf-kit.dev
# Your OpenAI model IDs stop on 23 October, so map each one before then
Your app can keep calling a model ID that OpenAI stops serving on 23 October 2026. OpenAI's deprecations page lists a replacement for each one, and most of the table shares that single date.
## What the OpenAI page says
The page has a section headed "2026-04-22: Legacy GPT model snapshots." It lists each snapshot with a shutdown date of October 23, 2026 and a substitute model. The page does not say that requests will fail. It says: "At the time of the shut down, the model or endpoint will no longer be accessible." A call to a model that is no longer accessible cannot succeed, so treat the date as the end of that ID.
The page also has a separate section for April 2027. It says: "The following models are deprecated and will be removed from the API on April 1, 2027, with six months' notice." That list names GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.4-Nano, and it is not part of this October deadline. If you want that one, read the April 2027 migration checklist.
The rules below are ours, and they are labelled as ours.
## The snapshots that stop on 23 October
The table below is taken from the page. Where the page lists an alias next to a snapshot, the alias is in brackets. Fine-tuned models have their own table, which names a recommended base model rather than a direct replacement.
|Model ID|Replacement on the page|Note|
|`gpt-3.5-turbo-0125` (`gpt-3.5-turbo`)|`gpt-5.6-terra`|Alias listed too|
|`gpt-4-0613` (`gpt-4`)|`gpt-5.6-sol`|Alias listed too|
|`gpt-4-1106-preview`|`gpt-5.6-sol`||
|`gpt-4-turbo` (`gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09`)|`gpt-5.6-sol`||
|`gpt-4.1-nano` (`gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`)|`gpt-5.6-luna`||
|`gpt-4o-2024-05-13`|`gpt-5.6-sol`||
|`gpt-image-1`|`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare`|Image model, two options listed|
|`o1` (`o1-2024-12-17`)|`gpt-5.6-sol`||
|`o1-pro` (`o1-pro-2025-03-19`)|`gpt-5.6-sol` with `reasoning.mode: pro`|The page lists the mode setting|
|`o3-mini` (`o3-mini-2025-01-31`)|`gpt-5.6-sol`||
|`o4-mini` (`o4-mini-2025-04-16`)|`gpt-5.6-terra`||
|`ft-o4-mini-2025-04-16`|`gpt-5.6-terra`|Fine-tuned snapshot|
The fine-tuned table lists five more: `ft-gpt-3.5-turbo` and `ft-babbage-002` and `ft-davinci-002` take `gpt-5.6-terra` as the base model, `ft-gpt-4` takes `gpt-5.6-sol`, and `ft-gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14` takes `gpt-5.6-luna`. The table names a base model for each one, so a fine-tuned app means retraining on that base. Your training data and the new base model are a separate job.
## Find every ID in your code
Search the repository for the model strings in the table above, and search for the aliases too. A string like `gpt-4` can match more than one place, so read each hit. Check the environment files, the CI secrets, the admin settings and any prompt store you keep outside the repo, because a model ID often lives in one of those and not in the code.
Keep the IDs in one config file. Our rule is one place per model choice, so a switch touches one line rather than a dozen call sites. The map can be as small as this:
```
// model choices, in one place
export const MODELS = {
  chat: "gpt-5.6-sol",
  cheap: "gpt-5.6-luna",
} as const
```
Name the purpose, not the model. A name like `chat` survives the next migration, and a name like `gpt4` does not.
## Test behavior, not only the ID
A replacement ID that the page lists tells you where to point the call. It does not tell you that your prompts produce the same output. The page does not describe output parity between the old and new models, so do not assume it.
